$comment: Dependency vulnerability policy (issue #1521).
THRESHOLD. `failOn` is what makes this gate adoptable. Failing on all 45 open alerts would
have meant a gate that is red on the day it lands, and a gate that is always red gets
bypassed — which is how the repo went without one at all. Critical fails at any scope; high
fails on the runtime path only. 32 of the 45 are development-scope and none of those is
critical, so they are reported by Dependabot and do not block a merge.
ACCEPTANCES ARE TIME-BOXED, NOT PERMANENT. Each one needs a reason, the issue tracking its
removal, and a date it stops working. The expiry is the point: an acceptance with no end date
is a silenced alert, and the gate exists because silence is what let 45 accumulate. When one
expires the gate fails and the choice comes back — fix it, or renew it deliberately.
THE LIST MUST ONLY EVER SHRINK. D-04 removes an entry that no longer matches an open alert, so
a stale excuse cannot sit here hiding the next real finding. Same rule as LEGACY_COLLISIONS
under the spec registry's S-04.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. The 12 OpenZeppelin alerts (#1520) are not accepted, because
they never reach the threshold: they are development-scope and not critical. They describe an
OZ 4.7.3 copy nested under @chainlink/contracts -> @arbitrum/nitro-contracts that solc never
reads: the four chainlink paths contracts/ imports close over 11 files with NO non-relative
imports at all, so that closure cannot reach node_modules. (An earlier draft said nitro is
"reachable only from automation/**" -- false, and corrected before any alert carried it; see
dismissals.json.) They should be DISMISSED on the alert itself, which is where the reasoning
belongs; an acceptance here would record them as tolerated risk, which is a different and
wrong claim. That dismissal is declared in `dismissals.json` and executed by
`npm run dismiss:alerts`, so the criteria that selected those twelve are reviewable — which a
click is not.

acceptances.reason: Nested axios@1.16.0 under @coinbase/cdp-sdk, reached via wagmi -> @wagmi/connectors -> @base-org/account. The root install is already 1.20.0 and outside every advisory range, so no direct bump clears it: the intermediate has to loosen its pin or we add an override. Tracked in #1519 for Iteration 6.

toml@3.0.0 arrives through @trezor/blockchain-link -> @stellar/stellar-sdk, i.e. the spec-085 hardware-wallet seam. Prototype pollution reachable only by parsing an attacker-supplied TOML document, which that path does not do; the SDK is lazy-loaded behind connectHardware. Tracked in #1519.

Same toml@3.0.0 copy as above via the Trezor SDK. Uncontrolled recursion is a denial of service against the parser, and the only documents it parses are ones the vendor SDK itself supplies. Fixed together with the sibling advisory in #1519.
